items.title: Ellis Marsalis — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: The interviewee discusses Dave Brubeck's music (referencing Desmond as the composer of 'Blue Rondo a la Turk') in the context of teaching materials and academic resistance, stating 'I know – in a way, I know it’s difficult... I’ve gone through experiences talking to the chairman... Me and my friend

ctx.x: . . . Desmond, playing Blue Rondo a la Turk, and saying, “Man, maybe you can check this out,” but without fully understanding, hey, this cat is out of another tradition. What he did was super, super bad. He had a choir that was killin’. After a while, you begin to say, wait a minute. You can’t convince these people to do anything other than whatever it is that they’re doing. I remember my son Ellis told me an anecdote. He say they had a young Japanese farmer who had studied rice growing. He had this farm that…
What do you mean by that? I know what Socratic and dialogue, etc., etc. What do you mean by . . . ?
